title: Grade 11 Physics — Work, Energy and Power
description: Work-energy theorem, conservation of energy, power, and collisions
subject: physics

questions.question: Work done by a force F on a displacement d is: W = ?
options: F d cos θ (where θ is angle between F and d)
questions.explanation: W = F·d·cos θ (dot product). When force is parallel to displacement: W = Fd (cos 0° = 1). Perpendicular: W = 0 (cos 90° = 0). Opposite: W = −Fd (cos 180° = −1).

questions.question: The Work-Energy Theorem states:
options: Work done = change in potential energy
Net work done on an object = change in its kinetic energy (W_net = ΔKE)
questions.explanation: Work-Energy Theorem: W_net = KE_final − KE_initial = ΔKE. All work done by all forces on the object equals the change in its kinetic energy. Derivation: use F=ma and v²=u²+2as.

questions.question: A 4 kg block is pushed 5 m by a 20 N force on a frictionless surface. The kinetic energy gained is:
questions.explanation: W = Fd cos0° = 20 × 5 = 100 J. By Work-Energy Theorem: ΔKE = 100 J.

questions.question: The potential energy stored in a spring compressed by x is: (k = spring constant)
questions.explanation: Elastic potential energy: PE = ½kx². By Hooke's Law, F = kx. Work done against this force from 0 to x: W = ∫kx dx = ½kx².

questions.question: Conservation of mechanical energy applies when:
options: Only conservative forces act (no friction or air resistance)
An object is in free fall only
questions.explanation: Mechanical energy (KE + PE) is conserved when only CONSERVATIVE forces (gravity, spring) act. Non-conservative forces (friction) convert mechanical energy to heat, causing mechanical energy to decrease.

questions.question: A 2 kg ball falls from height 5 m. Its speed just before hitting the ground is: (g = 10 m/s²)
questions.explanation: By energy conservation: mgh = ½mv² → v² = 2gh = 2×10×5 = 100 → v = 10 m/s.

questions.question: Power is defined as:
options: Work done / time (rate of doing work)
questions.explanation: Power P = W/t = work done per unit time. Also P = F·v (force × velocity). SI unit: Watt (W) = 1 J/s. Horsepower: 1 hp = 746 W.

questions.question: A motor lifts 100 kg by 10 m in 20 s. The power of the motor is: (g = 10 m/s²)
In a perfectly elastic collision:
options: Both momentum and kinetic energy are conserved
questions.explanation: Elastic collision: BOTH momentum AND kinetic energy are conserved. Inelastic collision: only momentum is conserved; KE decreases (converted to heat, sound). Perfectly inelastic: objects stick together.

questions.question: In a perfectly inelastic collision between equal masses (m) where one is at rest:
options: They move together with half the initial velocity
questions.explanation: By momentum conservation: mv = (m+m)v' → v' = v/2. Equal masses in perfectly inelastic collision: combined object moves with v/2. KE after = ½(2m)(v/2)² = mv²/4 = KE_before/2 (50% loss).

questions.question: A force does negative work when:
questions.explanation: W = Fd cos θ. When θ = 180°: W = Fd cos180° = −Fd (negative). Example: friction always does negative work on moving objects (opposes displacement).

questions.question: The kinetic energy of a body of mass m moving with velocity v is:
questions.explanation: KE = ½mv². Derives from work-energy theorem: F = ma, v² = u²+2as → W = Fs = mas = ½mv². Unit: Joule (J).

questions.question: If the momentum of a body is doubled, its kinetic energy becomes:
questions.explanation: KE = p²/2m. If p → 2p: KE_new = (2p)²/2m = 4p²/2m = 4 KE. Doubling momentum quadruples kinetic energy.

questions.question: A 60 kg person climbs stairs (height 4 m) in 8 s. The power exerted is: (g = 10 m/s²)
A bullet of mass 20 g moving at 500 m/s embeds in a block of 980 g at rest. The common velocity is:
questions.explanation: Momentum conservation: 0.02 × 500 = (0.02 + 0.98) × v → 10 = 1 × v → v = 10 m/s.
